assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I am writing to ask you not to make community service a rule for every student. Service helps people, but it turns into a chore when it is forced.

My friend Dana tutors second graders in reading every Thursday. She goes because she picked it, and the kids can tell. Now think about a student who only goes to get a form signed. He watches the clock the whole hour. The kid he is with sees that, and then the hour is a waste for both of them.

Time is the other thing. Some of my classmates work after school so their families can pay bills. Others watch their little brothers and sisters until a parent gets home at seven. They are tired by then. A set number of hours would hit them the most, because they have the least room in their week.

You could post openings and let people sign up on their own. Some of us would do it. If it is a rule, the rest of us will just count the hours and resent it.

Sincerely,
A student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I heard that you might make community service required for every student. I think that is a bad idea. Helping people is good but if you force us to do it then it is just like more homework.

My friend Dana tutors second graders in reading every Thursday. She does it because she likes those kids a lot, and they can tell. But what if somebody only goes because he needs his form signed? He would probably just look at the clock the whole time. The little kid would know he didn't want to be there and then nobody gets anything out of it.

Also some kids don't have time. There are kids in my class who have jobs after school because their family needs the money. Other kids have to watch their little brothers and sisters until their mom gets home at like seven. They don't have extra hours so the rule would be hardest on them, and that isn't fair.

I think you should just make it easier to volunteer instead. You could put up a list of places that need help and give credit to the people who do it. Then a lot of us would sign up anyway.

Sincerely,
A student
